source.title: The Geometric Wall: Manifold Structure Predicts Layerwise Sparse Autoencoder Scaling Laws
source.authors: Eslam Zaher; M. Trzaskowski; Quan Nguyen; Fred Roosta

record.tranche_reason: The study examines geometry-dependent sparse-autoencoder reconstruction scaling, but does not test feature overlap, superposition, polysemanticity, feature sparsity or importance, or feature dimensionality as described in the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper argues that a globally linear sparse dictionary can mismatch curved activation manifolds and reports SAE reconstruction-scaling results. Those results do not measure superposition or the feature and neuron properties in the claim versions. The geometry-conditioned scaling and floor results are recorded as related findings under fits_no_version. It cites Toy Models of Superposition as background, but reports no results from that work.
record.test_reason: The study regresses SAE width-scaling exponents and fitted reconstruction floors on activation-manifold geometry in Gemma 2 2B and 9B. It never measures feature overlap, interference, polysemantic neurons, capacity allocation, feature recovery, SAE feature stability, or feature dimensionality. Reconstruction-scaling behaviour is a related but different construct. The curved-manifold argument against flat sparse codes is interpretive and is not tied to a measure of what the SAE features are, so it does not test V5 or V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors also frame the SAE limit as a geometry-dependent wall rather than a finite-resource ceiling. They state they are not claiming SAEs are unsuitable for interpretability.
record.recipe_differences: This is an empirical SAE scaling study on Gemma 2 activation manifolds, not a toy-network superposition experiment or reproduction of the Toy Models of Superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: For Gemma 2 9B, curvature-only LOO R2 for the exponent regression decreases from 0.92 at k=16 to 0.85 at k=75. The authors also state that absolute fitted exponents are conditional on the released width-dependent SAE training schedule.

fits_no_version.finding: In Gemma 2 2B and 9B, multi-scale curvature of the activation manifold predicts per-layer SAE width-scaling exponents (LOO R2 0.976 and 0.869), and the relation transfers across models (transfer R2 0.920 and 0.970). At six showcase layers, fitted asymptotic reconstruction floors rank with intrinsic dimension and curvature.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For Gemma Scope JumpReLU SAEs on Gemma 2, activation-manifold curvature and intrinsic dimension predict layerwise reconstruction scaling and fitted reconstruction floors.

record.problems: The study uses publicly released SAEs with a width-dependent training budget rather than convergence-matched training. The all-layer fits use only two shared backbone widths; asymptotic floors are identifiable only at six showcase layers. Geometric summaries are k-NN proxies rather than direct pullback-metric computations. The reported results concern SAE reconstruction and do not directly assess feature recovery, feature overlap, or feature dimensionality.

untested.parts: No toy networks; no feature-direction geometry, sparsity-driven phase transition or regular polytopes measured.
No neuron-level polysemanticity or capacity-allocation measurement.
No measurement of alternative origins of polysemantic neurons.
Uses released SAEs but reports only reconstruction NMSE scaling, not whether sparse features are recovered or spread across neurons.
Completeness, stability and canonicity of SAE features are not measured. Reconstruction floors are fitted only at six layers on SAEs trained with a width-dependent schedule.
No test of whether features are 1-D or multi-dimensional. Curvature is measured on the whole activation cloud, not on individual features.

record.verdict_notes: The H0 baseline LOO R2 values (-0.049, -0.082) are finite-sample constants for an intercept-only model, not empirical baselines. The floors (r5-r10) come from only six layers on SAEs not trained to convergence. Appendix I argues flat sparse dictionaries are a first-order approximation; this could be read as bearing on V5 completeness, but it is interpretation, not a measurement of SAE features, so no verdict is given. Toy Models of Superposition is cited only as background for the linear representation hypothesis.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks with more sparse features than dimensions; overlapping nearly orthogonal feature directions; sparsity-dependent transitions and regular geometry.
Whether capacity pressure causes polysemanticity or determines which features receive dedicated dimensions.
Whether polysemantic neurons arise through mechanisms other than capacity pressure.
Whether LLM features are distributed across neurons or whether SAEs recover sparse features; the paper measures SAE reconstruction error, not feature recovery or neuron-feature distribution.
Whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units of model representations.
Whether represented features are one-dimensional directions or multidimensional structures.

relation.reason: The study's own floor results and geometric argument bear on V5 completeness, beyond discussing prior superposition work. Feature stability and canonicity remain untested.

tranche.reason: Section 5 and Appendices E/I offer a specific argument that sparse linear SAE decompositions remain incomplete, supported by fitted reconstruction floors. Appendix I explicitly rejects their status as asymptotically correct decompositions. This bears on V5 completeness; T5 includes specific arguments requiring a version to be qualified.

source_check.notes: The omitted V5 completeness argument warrants consideration alongside r5–r10; it does not establish feature instability or noncanonicity. Floors are fitted extrapolations at fixed sparsity, and scaling estimates describe the released width-dependent SAE training schedule.
